concepts.name: Readability as code goal
aliases: code is read more than written
concepts.summary: Explain why code is read far more often than it is written and why readable code lowers the cost of change.

concepts.name: Intention-revealing names
concepts.summary: Choose variable, function and class names that state what a thing is or does without needing a comment.

concepts.name: Consistent formatting and layout
concepts.summary: Recall how consistent indentation, spacing and line length help readers see code structure.

concepts.name: Small single-purpose functions
concepts.summary: Explain why a function should do one thing and be short enough to understand at a glance.

concepts.name: Magic numbers and named constants
concepts.summary: Recognise unexplained literal values and understand why replacing them with named constants clarifies meaning.

concepts.name: Refactoring definition
concepts.summary: State that refactoring changes internal structure without changing observable behavior.

concepts.name: Comments versus self-explaining code
concepts.summary: Distinguish comments that explain why from comments that merely restate or excuse unclear code.

misconceptions.text: Short names are better because they are quicker to type.
Clean code just means code that looks neat and is heavily commented.
Refactoring means rewriting code or adding features while tidying up.

concepts.name: Extract Function move
concepts.summary: Pull a coherent block of code into a well-named function and replace the original with a call.

concepts.name: Rename refactoring
concepts.summary: Rename identifiers across the code, ideally with tool support, to better express intent.

concepts.name: Duplicated code and DRY
concepts.summary: Spot repeated logic and consolidate it into a single shared function or constant.

concepts.name: Basic code smells
concepts.summary: Recognise common smells such as long functions, long parameter lists, duplicated code and dead code as signals to investigate.

concepts.name: Tests as refactoring safety net
concepts.summary: Run existing tests before and after each small change to confirm behavior stays the same.

concepts.name: Small incremental steps
concepts.summary: Break a restructuring into tiny steps, each leaving the code working, instead of one big change.

concepts.name: Guard clauses and nesting reduction
aliases: replace nested conditional with guard clauses
concepts.summary: Flatten deeply nested conditionals by handling edge cases early with guard clauses.

concepts.name: Removing dead code
concepts.summary: Delete unused variables, functions and commented-out code, relying on version control to recover it.

misconceptions.text: Any code smell is a bug that must be fixed immediately.
If the code runs and passes tests, it does not need refactoring.
Any two similar-looking pieces of code should always be merged.

concepts.name: Object-oriented and structural smells
concepts.summary: Diagnose smells like feature envy, large classes, primitive obsession and shotgun surgery and relate each to the design problem behind it.

concepts.name: Single Responsibility and cohesion
concepts.summary: Analyse whether a class or module has one reason to change and split it when responsibilities are mixed.

concepts.name: Move and Extract Class
concepts.summary: Relocate behavior or data to the class where it belongs and extract new classes to restore cohesion.

concepts.name: Replace conditional with polymorphism
concepts.summary: Replace repeated type-based conditionals with polymorphic objects or strategies when variants keep growing.

concepts.name: Coupling and dependency reduction
concepts.summary: Analyse how dependencies between units make change costly and reduce them with narrower interfaces and fewer reach-through calls.

concepts.name: Introduce parameter object
concepts.summary: Group parameters that travel together into one object to shorten signatures and give the concept a name.

concepts.name: Characterization tests for legacy code
concepts.summary: Write tests that capture current behavior of untested code so it can be refactored safely.

concepts.name: Error handling clarity
concepts.summary: Separate error handling from main logic and use exceptions or explicit result types instead of ambiguous return codes.

misconceptions.text: Single Responsibility means a class should have only one method.
Every switch statement should be replaced with polymorphism.
Legacy code without tests cannot be refactored until it is rewritten.

concepts.name: Refactoring trade-off evaluation
concepts.summary: Judge whether a refactoring is worth its cost, weighing upcoming change, risk, and team context.

concepts.name: Preparatory and opportunistic refactoring
concepts.summary: Choose when to refactor before a feature, during it, or in a separate pass, and keep refactoring commits separate from behavior changes.

concepts.name: Branch by abstraction and seams
concepts.summary: Use seams and parallel-change techniques to migrate code or interfaces in steps while the system keeps working.

concepts.name: Hotspot and metrics analysis
concepts.summary: Combine change frequency from history with complexity measures to find where refactoring pays off, while treating metrics as hints.

concepts.name: Technical debt management
concepts.summary: Distinguish deliberate from accidental debt and prioritise paydown by interest paid in slowed work and defects.

concepts.name: Over-abstraction and premature generalisation
concepts.summary: Evaluate when an abstraction or deduplication adds more coupling than it removes and inline it back.

concepts.name: Refactoring in code review
concepts.summary: Assess a change for readability and design quality and give actionable feedback that separates preference from real maintainability issues.

misconceptions.text: Code metrics such as complexity scores objectively show which code is bad.
Technical debt is just bad code written by careless developers.
Removing all duplication is always an improvement.

concepts.name: Large-scale architectural refactoring
concepts.summary: Design an incremental migration strategy that reshapes system structure while continuously delivering.

concepts.name: Refactoring strategy design
concepts.summary: Create a plan that sequences refactorings, safety nets and checkpoints to reach a target design across teams.

concepts.name: Team code quality standards
concepts.summary: Establish team conventions, automated linting and review practices that sustain quality without stifling judgment.

concepts.name: Automated refactoring tooling
concepts.summary: Evaluate and build automated, syntax-aware transformations for safe changes across a large codebase.

concepts.name: Design principles trade-off critique
concepts.summary: Critique how principles like DRY, SRP and abstraction conflict in context and justify a design choice.

concepts.name: Changeability and cost-of-change reasoning
concepts.summary: Assess which design decisions are costly to reverse and focus structure and flexibility there.

concepts.name: Coaching clean code practice
concepts.summary: Develop others' refactoring judgment through pairing, katas and feedback that builds shared standards.

misconceptions.text: A large, rewrite-from-scratch project is a safer way to fix a messy system than incremental refactoring.
Enforcing strict linting rules and style guides is enough to produce maintainable code.
Following clean code principles consistently always yields the best design.
